newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA SEEKS ROLE IN DECISION-MAKING WITH NATO.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA SEEKS ROLE IN DECISION-MAKING WITH NATO.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov urged NATO on Wednesday to step up efforts to work out a special relationship with Moscow and demanded the right to joint decision-making with the Western alliance on some issues.

Primakov told Itar-Tass news agency that Russia remained firmly opposed to NATO's plans to expand eastwards. But he made clear that some of its fears would be eased if a new deal was reached governing conventional arms in Europe and a mechanism was created to make joint decisions on issues involving Russia.
Primakov said efforts made by NATO to address Russia's concerns and work out a special relationship had been welcome but had not gone far enough.
"They are steps in the right direction, but they are partial and insufficient," he told Tass.

Primakov's remarks continued the tough line Moscow has adopted over NATO's expansion plans, which it says would threaten its security and create new divisions in Europe. But they also suggested there remained some room for manoeuvre.

He said Moscow would measure the seriousness of NATO's proposal to work out its new relationship with Russia by progress in renegotiating the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty governing non-nuclear arms.
